description: Facts read in the three.js source shipped in the npm package the repo pins (package.json three ^0.186.1, package-lock 0.186.1). Grade A: primary source read. Line numbers are those of the unpacked tarball. These facts fix the batching / LOD / draw-call rules the technical spec builds on.

facts.fact: One geometry + material(s) drawn N times with different transforms in one draw call (renderInstances). instanceMatrix = InstancedBufferAttribute(Float32Array(count * 16), 16) -> 64 bytes per instance. setColorAt lazily allocates instanceColor = Float32Array(count * 3) -> 12 bytes per instance. Frustum culling is per InstancedMesh (one bounding sphere over all instances, computeBoundingSphere), not per instance.

Multi-draw batch of DIFFERENT geometries sharing one material: new BatchedMesh(maxInstanceCount, maxVertexCount, maxIndexCount = 2 * maxVertexCount, material); addGeometry / addInstance / setMatrixAt / setColorAt. perObjectFrustumCulled = true (each instance culled), sortObjects = true (front-to-back opaque, back-to-front transparent). Per-instance data lives in float textures: matrices texture side = max(4, ceil(sqrt(4 * maxInstanceCount) / 4) * 4) RGBA32F; colours texture side = ceil(sqrt(maxInstanceCount)) RGBA32F; indirect texture side = ceil(sqrt(maxInstanceCount)) R32UI.

renderer.info.render.calls is incremented once per info.update. A BatchedMesh with WEBGL_multi_draw issues ONE multiDrawElementsWEBGL and counts ONE call; WITHOUT the extension the renderer loops renderer.render once per visible instance (one call each). An InstancedMesh counts one call. So a deterministic draw-call budget must state whether WEBGL_multi_draw is present.

addLevel(object, distance = 0, hysteresis = 0); levels sorted by distance. update(camera): distance = |cameraWorldPos - lodWorldPos| / camera.zoom; level i is shown when distance >= levels[i].distance, reduced by levels[i].distance * hysteresis while that level is currently visible (so it switches back only below distance * (1 - hysteresis)). One LOD object per entity -> per-entity Object3D; for 1e5+ components the LOD choice must be done per batch (instance buckets), not with THREE.LOD objects.

Experimental SceneOptimizer.toBatchedMesh groups meshes by batchKey = materialPropertiesHash + attributesSignature, creates one BatchedMesh per group and reports drawCalls = batchGroups.size + singleGroups.size. toInstancingMesh() throws 'not implemented yet'. Confirms the batching key llull adopts: (material class, vertex-attribute layout) for unique geometry; (prototype geometry, material class) for instancing.
EdgesGeometry(geometry, thresholdAngle = 1) draws an edge only where adjacent face normals differ by more than thresholdAngle degrees.
Ambient occlusion (SSAO, SAO, GTAO), outlines, SMAA / TAA, cascaded shadow maps and first-person / fly / pointer-lock controls ship with three r186 as addons; wide lines (Line2) exist for redlines.

computeBatchedBoundsTree / acceleratedRaycast patch BatchedMesh; ObjectBVH builds a scene-wide BVH over objects and has a frustum-culling example (API marked as recent / may change). llull's bvhSetup.ts patches Mesh only, not InstancedMesh / BatchedMesh.

Detailed = THREE.LOD wrapper (distances[], hysteresis); PerformanceMonitor reports fps / factor with onIncline / onDecline; AdaptiveDpr lowers the pixel ratio on regression. All are per-object helpers: usable for the review shell, not for 1e6 components.
